rule: written 2026-10-08 before the run (blue.py's header). Plain Default-vs-Default decisive drafts, normal queue folders, every night on disk. A both-blue draft is 0.5 for blue by construction, so blue's deficit is its deficit in one-blue drafts; contention there is the blue cards the non-blue seat took (low band: at or under the cube's 25th percentile; high band: at or over its 75th). (b) Forge plays blue worse is shown when, in the low band, blue's log-odds at equal deck quality (logit on the two decks' lab deck scores as within-cube z-scores, plus who was on the play) has a 95% interval entirely below 0. The verdict is both, (a), (b), or neither shown (no interval clears), pooled over the cubes; per-cube verdicts are description only

Per cube (Vintage, Synergy), cards = nonland cards with 500+ games in hand in ForgeCoach@bd51ce3's <cube>.human.json and at least one lab game in both arms; rho = Spearman (average ranks) between the arm's per-card lab win rate (meta.json wins / games) and the human GIH WR (gihW / gih); difference rho(B) - rho(A), B = search-v2 vs search-v2, A = Forge Default vs Forge Default on the same draft seeds; paired bootstrap over cards, 10,000 resamples, default_rng(20261006), percentile 95% interval. title: B3, the win chance on human games: Platt recalibration of the frozen r17 evaluator on 17Lands' Powered Cube replays (dev half), tested on the held-out half, with the human/Forge relative slope a coach would need (D415)
decides: whether ForgeCoach's win chance gets a "human" calibration (the relative human/Forge transform in b3-human-calibration.json) for games against people and the search AI, and in which form (global or per turn band)
hypothesis: J063's reliability table showed the r17 win chance too extreme on human games (fitted slope about 0.82), so a Platt fit on the dev half lowers held-out log-loss; part of that slope is r17's own over-confidence on Forge's games (J063: "0.957" was 0.895), so the relative slope (human / Forge) is expected nearer 1 than the absolute one, and whether its interval excludes 1 is open
rule: D415, human_calib.py CALIB_RULE. Population: PremierDraft's whole file, D359's test half, both perspectives, turn >= 3, final half-turn dropped, share >= 0.5; the r17 evaluator frozen (J063's var/ml/models/r17-vintage-n1.json, sha256 recorded). PASS when log-loss(uncalibrated) - log-loss(global Platt fitted on the dev half) > 0 with the lower end of its 95% percentile interval (2,000 resamples over test games, seed 20261008) above 0, on >= 2,000 games and 10,000 rows; fewer is FAIL (underpowered); a partial download, a sample, one perspective or another file is NO VERDICT. Per-band form only when log-loss(global) - log-loss(bands) has its interval above 0. Coach use = relative only on a PASS with a Forge-side fit of >= 2,000 rows and 20 deck pairs, both slopes positive, and the relative slope's 95% interval excluding 1; else none
publicTitle: Win chance calibration on human games
publicDecides: Recalibrate the win chance for games against people

title: B2, deckbuilder choices: from 800 lab drafts each of Vintage 180 and Evan's cube (seeds 812,000,001+), every seat's pool built by ForgeCoach's deck assistant and a few one-decision variants (16 / 17 / 18 lands, the splash cut) plus the lab's and Forge's own builds, each played against the other seat's lab deck; paired by pool, Forge Default vs Forge Default on all of them and search-v2 vs search-v2 on 120 drafts a cube as a sign check
decides: whether ForgeCoach's deck assistant changes its land count (16 vs 17) or its splash, and how its builds compare with the lab's and Forge's; 18 lands goes to Justin, never changed by this job
hypothesis: ForgeCoach's builder (lab win rates + 17Lands, Justin's two colours + a <=3-card splash on 16-17 lands) should beat Forge's BoosterDeckBuilder clearly (Forge leaves out colourless lands and low-rated cards and pads thin pools) and the lab builder slightly; one land or the splash is a small effect, a few points at most, so most contrasts may be not shown at this size
rule: written 2026-10-10 before any J121 game was played (variants.ts, the read). Unit: a focus pool = one seat of one lab draft; each of its decks plays 2 games (one per seat) against the OTHER seat's lab deck, the same opponent for every variant; a game scores 1/0, a draw or timeout 1/2, an engine error is left out; per pool the variant's mean minus the reference's, averaged within the draft (its two seats), then over drafts; normal 95% and 99% intervals. Five primary contrasts on the Forge Default arm (all drafts, both cubes pooled): lands16 = 16 minus 17 lands and lands18 = 18 minus 17 lands (ForgeCoach's colours and splash, one spell per land, the builder's own pick), nosplash = ForgeCoach's splash swapped for on-colour spells minus ForgeCoach's deck (pools where it splashes), lab = the lab builder minus ForgeCoach, forge = Forge's builder minus ForgeCoach. A contrast is SHOWN when its 99% interval excludes 0 (five contrasts, about 5% familywise). lands16, lands18 and nosplash also need the search-v2 arm's point estimate on the same side, else NOT SHOWN. Decisions: lands16 shown for 16 -> a follow-up makes 16 the deck assistant's default (the meta's land table still first); shown for 17 -> it drops its low-curve 16-land rule. nosplash shown for the cut -> a follow-up stops the deck assistant's splashes; shown for the splash -> it keeps them. lands18 shown for 18 -> reported to Justin (his rule keeps 18 for thin pools), nothing changes. lab / forge -> which builder wins, nothing changes by itself. Everything else: no change. An interval that includes 0 is not shown, never no effect

rule: written 2026-10-14 before any J125 game was played. title: B1, distilling search-v2 into a fast policy: 1,800 lab games of Vintage 180, Evan's cube and Synergy with search-v2 in both seats and D435's row exporter on (seeds 814,000,001+), one small candidate scorer per decision kind trained on what search-v2 played (split by game, 80/10/10), its held-out top-1 agreement per kind, then two fixed 1,200-game matches (600 mirrored pairs, D398): distilled vs search-v2 and distilled vs Forge Default
decides: whether the distilled policy (search-v2's own candidates at priority, attack and block, scored by a small model trained on search-v2's choices, no rollout) ships as a lab policy, a ladder player for faster lab games and a candidate for the live hint
hypothesis: search-v2 keeps Forge's answer at about 80-86% of the decisions it searches (J115, J116: it changes 20% of priority plays, 14% of attacks, 16-17% of blocks), so the always-Forge baseline agrees about 82% of the time and the question is how many of the other 18% a small model recovers; a distilled seat that recovers few of them plays close to Forge Default plus outlets, which search-v2 beats, so a score of 0.45-0.49 against search-v2 is the plausible range and SHIP is not the expected outcome; the speed side is near certain (the smoke: 3.2 ms a decision against search-v2's 715 ms)
rule: written 2026-10-14 before any J126 row was generated. SHIP the distilled player (search-v2-distill-<sha12>, kind search-distill, registered by distill.py register from this run's model) as a lab policy when ALL of (1) its fixed match against search-v1-anytime (search-v2) is complete, 1,200 of 1,200 games; (2) it is not shown worse than search-v2 by more than 0.03 in score: the lower end of the 95% interval on its score in that match (var/ai-ladder/match-J126-search.json, `lo`) is at least 0.47; (3) it is at least 10 times faster per decision: search-v2's mean decision time over the held-out TEST decisions of this run's rows (p + a + b, rows with a search fallback excluded; metrics.json test.searchMsMean) divided by the distilled seat's mean decision time in that same match (aSearch.msPerDecision: p + a + b, the same span, from before the candidates are generated to the verdict) is at least 10. Otherwise NOT SHOWN, naming the part that failed. distill.py verdict computes it (MARGIN 0.03, SPEEDUP 10). Fixed before the data: the split (by game, sha256("J126|<game key>") mod 100, the key being the rows folder (one a cube) and the lab's lab:<seed>:g<n>: 0-79 train, 80-89 val, 90-99 test), the exclusions (a row whose search fell back; a game without an ok end line), the model and its settings (distill.py train's defaults at the pinned commit: hidden 32, at most 40 epochs, patience 4 on validation loss, Adam lr 0.003, L2 0.0001, batch 512, seed 126, at least 200 training decisions for a kind to get a head), and that nothing is tuned on the test split. The agreement report and the match against Forge Default decide nothing: both are reported. An interval whose lower end is under 0.47 is "not shown non-inferior", never "worse"; a match that stopped early gives no verdict
publicTitle: Distilled search policy: train and two fixed matches
publicDecides: Ship a distilled search policy for lab games

decides: whether ForgeCoach shows the owner a "Your leaks" page (each leak's example moments linked to the replay), and from which kinds; nothing ships from this job by itself

rule: written 2026-10-15 before any of his decisions was graded at J129's settings; D438 and tools/leaks/rule.ts RULE (copied into leaks.json). title: The compute curve: three fixed 1,200-game matches (600 mirrored pairs each, D398, the confirm set, no stopping rule) in one night: (a) search-v1-anytime (search-v2, today's main) vs forge-default, the re-anchor; (b) search-v2-ms6000-r48 vs search-v2, the rule's match; (c) search-v2-ms3000-r24 vs search-v2, read beside; the two new players are search-v2 with the wall-clock budget and the round cap raised together, 2x and 4x (D514)
decides: which lanes come next for the play AI (the play-AI review of 2026-11-05, §5): COMPUTE PAYS opens parallel rollouts or a faster copy (row 4) and a learned prior from per-option values (row 5); COMPUTE DOES NOT PAY closes both and points the work at the rollout policy instead; INCONCLUSIVE posts a 4,800-game confirmation of search-v2-ms6000-r48 against search-v2 first. It never decides the live seat, which stays search-v2 at 1.5 s (the owner: "a production model needs to be fast but we can experiment for testing")
hypothesis: the search is short of samples: at 1.5 s a searched decision takes ~907 ms and plays ~14-16 rollouts, 2-3 a candidate (J139; J131 16.2), 42% of its picks sit inside the runner-up's interval and 18% are more likely the worse of the two (J068). Three things point to compute paying: the anytime loop's +9.3 Elo [+2.5, +16.0] came from deciding the decisions the old loop handed back (J102, D412); on gate 2's set 12 rounds against 3 flip 4.4% of picks with regret(3) - regret(12) = +0.001 [-0.000, +0.003] a decision (J068), which, if it added up over ~23 searched decisions a game (a hypothesis), is about +16 Elo, +50 at the upper end; and no ladder match has ever been played at another budget. Against it: the rollouts play the opponent as Forge Default (D312) to the end of the turn, so more of them sharpen the same estimate, not a better one, and with the round cap raised with the budget the race still retires alternatives early, so 6 s with 48 rounds buys more rollouts than 1.5 s with 12 but perhaps not 4x (D514's pilot: the budget alone, with the 12-round cap, bought 1.41x the time and ~1.15x the rollouts). PAYS and INCONCLUSIVE are both plausible; DOES NOT PAY needs a point near +6 Elo or below
rule: written 2026-11-05 before any J194 game was played, from the play-AI review of 2026-11-05 §5 row 2, word for word: "COMPUTE PAYS if ms6000's lower end is above 0.5 and its point is ≥ +15 Elo. COMPUTE DOES NOT PAY if its upper end is below +20 Elo (0.529). Otherwise inconclusive: confirm with 4,800 games." Three fixed matches (D398, no stopping rule), each 1,200 games (150 batches of 8, 600 mirrored pairs) on the confirm deck set (tools/ai-bench/pairs-confirm.txt, 34 deck pairs never tuned on), in this order: (a) search-v1-anytime vs forge-default, var/ai-ladder/match-J194a.json; (b) search-v2-ms6000-r48 vs search-v1-anytime, var/ai-ladder/match-J194b.json; (c) search-v2-ms3000-r24 vs search-v1-anytime, var/ai-ladder/match-J194c.json. Each matchup is new, so each takes this host's match blocks 114,900,000-114,900,149: the same 600 deals for all three, and (a) the same deals as J101's search-v1 vs forge-default. In the quoted rule ms6000 is the player search-v2-ms6000-r48 (D514 replaced the budget-only arms before any game). title: Judge the judge -- does the language model's pick beat Forge's under STRONG continuation? The 82 move-atlas decisions (v1's confident rows) where both blind judges of round 2 (the board shown) picked the same option and it is not Forge's option 0, each played on D451's Forge map (Forge's AI on both seats, 40 branches an option, D498's redeal, D511's replay of the night's recorded game) for exactly two options, Forge's and the judges'; the 24 split decisions beside them as information; a pre-registered reading: KNOWLEDGE SHOWN, NOT SHOWN or INCONCLUSIVE. Needs the `--only` lane first (an atlas spine branched at given decisions and options)
decides: whether the outside-knowledge direction gets a design. KNOWLEDGE SHOWN (the judges' option is better under Forge continuation in a share of the untied decisions whose 95% lower end is above 0.5, AND the mean value gain, judges' option minus Forge's, has a 95% lower end above 0): a language model as candidate ranker or rollout policy, distilled for the nights, gets a design -- a lane with its own decision, never this job's; nothing in the seat or the atlas changes here. NOT SHOWN (the share's upper end below 0.5, or the gain's upper end below 0): the random/self-play direction alone; the outside-knowledge direction is closed for this population of decisions. INCONCLUSIVE (anything else): no design on this evidence; the random/self-play direction proceeds as the default and the outside-knowledge question stays open only for a new, larger set of judged decisions, never by re-reading these 82 (the owner may decide otherwise at the read). Round 2's 44% hit rate on the random map decides nothing either way: that map rewards chaos (the all-in attack) and punishes sound sequencing (pass the first main phase to attack, then cast), because everything after the forced option is played at random
hypothesis: information only, never read by a check. **What is already known on these decisions.** 12 of the 82 sit on the nights' Forge-map spines and already have both options' Forge maps at 40 branches (the release's rows): the judges' option is better on 6, worse on 2 and tied on 4, a mean gain of +0.005 [-0.070, +0.053] (this job's reader, 500-4,000-draw cluster bootstrap over their 8 spines); on the random map the same 12 read 12 better / 0 worse, +0.137 [+0.089, +0.173], and the per-decision rank correlation of the random-map gain with the Forge-map gain is 0.14. Round 2's own Forge-map read (24 rows, every confident row with a Forge map): the judges' picks 0.560 and 0.558 mean value against 0.557 for option 0 and 0.561 for a uniform pick. **What 82 decisions can see.** Resampling those 12 decisions' branch vectors to 82 decisions on the 46 spines gives a gain interval about +-0.023 wide on each side and a share interval about +-0.13: KNOWLEDGE SHOWN needs a true mean gain of about +0.03 or more (about one branch game in 40, on average, at every decision) with most untied decisions going the judges' way; NOT SHOWN needs a true loss of about -0.025; the 12's point (+0.005) reads INCONCLUSIVE. So INCONCLUSIVE is the likeliest reading and is not "no knowledge"; an interval that includes 0 is never "no effect". The random map's side will read strongly for the judges whatever the truth: these rows were chosen (the confident filter) because some option beat option 0 there, and the judges' option is the random map's best on 59 of the 82
rule: written 2026-11-08 before any J200 branch game was played, word for word: "On the valid tier-1 decisions, the SHARE is the decisions where the judges' option's Forge-map mean beats Forge's option 0's over decisions where they differ (ties excluded and counted), and the GAIN is the mean over all valid decisions of (judges' option's Forge-map mean - option 0's), each mean over the branch indices where both options have a score. Both carry a 95% interval from a two-level cluster bootstrap, 10,000 draws, seed 200: spines resampled with replacement, then each drawn decision's paired branch indices resampled with replacement. KNOWLEDGE SHOWN if shareLo > 0.5 and gainLo > 0. NOT SHOWN if shareHi < 0.5 or gainHi < 0. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. Read only when at least 74 of the 82 tier-1 decisions are valid; else INCOMPLETE, no verdict." A decision is VALID when J200's baseline game lists, decision for decision, what the night's listed (tokens, kind and turn: the same game, D511), its listing at d is the plan's tokens, every Forge unit of the decision finished with no replay divergence, and it has at least 30 paired Forge branches. A branch scores as the atlas scores it (win 1, draw or the turn cap or a timeout between steps 0.5, loss 0; D478); a row with an error or an unavailable option is no score (D470). The two readings cannot both hold (SHOWN implies shareHi > 0.5 and gainHi > 0); a share with no untied decision in a draw leaves that draw out of the share's interval (counted). The share's interval carries each decision's own branch noise, so a decision won by one branch game in 40 counts close to a coin flip and the interval can sit below its point; that is the rule, not a defect. Beside the reading, deciding nothing: the same share and gain on the random map (the night's rows of the same decisions and option pairs), by kind, on live decisions (either option's Forge mean strictly between 0.05 and 0.95), on the decisions both judges gave confidence 3, the per-decision Spearman correlation of the random-map gain with the Forge-map gain, the reproduction of the night's Forge rows on the decisions the night mapped (expected identical: the same position, the same branch seeds), and tier 2 (each judge's non-0 pick against option 0, and the two judges' picks against each other where both are non-0), all with the same bootstrap at 2,000 draws. All of it is computed by var/j200-tools/read.py exactly as written in the pilot

title: Judge the judge, unselected -- does J200's KNOWLEDGE SHOWN hold on decisions nobody chose? 160 move-atlas decisions drawn at random (seed 203, stratified by kind, no filter on confidence, disagreement or either map), each read blind by two judges for a first choice, a second choice and a confidence; set i (both judges on one option that is not Forge's) branched on D451's Forge map for Forge's option and theirs, exactly as J200; set ii (both judges on Forge's option) branched for Forge's option and their second choice, as a control; set iii (the judges split) recorded, not branched; two pre-registered readings: J200's rule on set i (KNOWLEDGE SHOWN, NOT SHOWN or INCONCLUSIVE) and the control on set ii (CONTROL HOLDS, FAILS or INCONCLUSIVE)
decides: whether J200's reading survives an unselected sample, and so what the outside-knowledge design (J200's `decides:`) may assume. KNOWLEDGE SHOWN on set i AND CONTROL HOLDS on set ii: the judges are a signal on decisions nobody chose -- where two agree against Forge their option is better under Forge continuation, and where they agree with Forge their own ranking still puts Forge's option above their second choice; the outside-knowledge design (a language model as candidate ranker or rollout policy, its own lane and decision, never this job's) goes ahead as a ranker, with set i's gain and the whole-sample gain as its expected size; nothing in the seat or the atlas changes here. KNOWLEDGE SHOWN without CONTROL HOLDS: the gain where two judges agree against Forge stands on an unselected sample, but the judges' ranking is not shown to separate options where they agree with Forge; the design goes ahead only as a disagreement filter (act where two judges agree against Forge, defer to Forge elsewhere), not as a general ranker. NOT SHOWN on set i: J200's 82 do not generalize; J200's reading is attributed to its selection (the confident filter) and the outside-knowledge direction closes for this population of decisions (the owner may decide otherwise at the read). INCONCLUSIVE: no design on this evidence; J200 stands as a selected-sample result and the question stays open only for a new, larger judged sample, never by re-reading these 160. INCOMPLETE (set i under 30 decisions planned, or fewer than 90% of them valid): no verdict. The control's reading alone decides nothing when set i is not SHOWN
hypothesis: information only, never read by a check. **What J200 showed.** On 82 selected decisions (the atlas's confident rows, both judges confidently against Forge) the judges' option beat Forge's under Forge continuation: share 0.642 [0.515, 0.767], gain +0.050 [+0.018, +0.082]; the random map read 0.963 on the same rows, its Spearman correlation with the Forge map per decision 0.088, so the selection toward the random map said little about the Forge map. **What changes here.** Nothing filters this sample: 29 of the 160 are confident rows, 31 partial (the futility rule stopped them with option 0 leading or tied), 38 screened (cut after 25 branches) and 62 complete; many decisions have options worth about the same (a land's ability, a pass against a castable spell that makes no difference), so set i's true gain is expected below J200's and ties above J200's 15 of 82. Judge A sided with Forge on 84 of 160 (52.5%), confidence 1/2/3 on 36/93/31. **What set i can see.** With about 60 decisions (A's 76 non-Forge picks times J200's two-judge agreement) the gain interval is about +-0.037 (J200's +-0.032 at 82, times sqrt(82/60)) and the share's about +-0.15: KNOWLEDGE SHOWN needs a true gain of about +0.04 or more; J200's +0.050 would read SHOWN a little more often than not. **The control.** Where both judges side with Forge, Forge's option against their second choice: if their ranking is signal, Forge's option should win there by about as much as the judges' option wins on set i; a control near zero says the judges' preferences among the options they did not pick are noise around 50%
rule: written 2026-11-09 before any J203 branch game was played, word for word: "PRIMARY (set i, J200's rule): on the valid set-i decisions, the SHARE is the decisions where the judges' option's Forge-map mean beats Forge's option 0's over decisions where they differ (ties excluded and counted), and the GAIN is the mean over all valid set-i decisions of (judges' option's Forge-map mean - option 0's), each mean over the branch indices where both options have a score. Both carry a 95% interval from a two-level cluster bootstrap, 10,000 draws, seed 203: spines resampled with replacement, then each drawn decision's paired branch indices resampled with replacement. KNOWLEDGE SHOWN if shareLo > 0.5 and gainLo > 0. NOT SHOWN if shareHi < 0.5 or gainHi < 0. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. Read only when set i has at least 30 valid decisions and at least 90% of its planned decisions (rounded up) are valid; else INCOMPLETE, no verdict. CONTROL (set ii): the same SHARE and GAIN with each decision's paired difference taken as option 0's Forge-map score minus the mean of the judges' distinct second choices' scores at that branch index (one second when both judges named the same, two when they differ), over the branch indices where all compared options have a score, the same bootstrap and seed. CONTROL HOLDS if shareLo > 0.5 and gainLo > 0. CONTROL FAILS if shareHi < 0.5 or gainHi < 0. Otherwise CONTROL INCONCLUSIVE; read under the same completeness condition on set ii, else INCOMPLETE. WHOLE SAMPLE, reported with the readings: each judge's agreement with Forge's option and with each other over all 160; the WHOLE GAIN, the mean over the valid decisions of sets i and ii of (the judges' first choice's Forge-map mean - option 0's), which is set i's paired differences and 0 on set ii, with the same bootstrap; and set i's gain minus set ii's control gain with a joint bootstrap (spines resampled once a draw for both sets), deciding nothing." A decision is VALID when J203's baseline game lists, decision for decision, what the night's listed (tokens, kind and turn: the same game, D511), its listing at d is the plan's tokens, every Forge unit of the decision finished with no replay divergence, and it has at least 30 paired Forge branches. A branch scores as the atlas scores it (win 1, draw or the turn cap or a timeout between steps 0.5, loss 0; D478); a row with an error or an unavailable option is no score (D470). Set iii (the judges split) is never branched and never read. The atlas's own checks (problems, frame logs, leak checks) are information beside the readings: the validity conditions above decide which decisions count, and the job's checks hold only the verdict file to the rule and the leak count to zero (J200's `problems == 0` gate, which failed J200 on one BranchTimeout inside one engine step of a valid decision, is not carried over). Beside the readings, deciding nothing (2,000 draws): the random map (the night's rows of the same decisions and options), by kind, by the label's status (confident rows, J200's population, against the rest), live decisions (any compared option's Forge mean strictly between 0.05 and 0.95), both judges at confidence 3, the Spearman correlation of the random-map difference with the Forge-map difference, and the reproduction of the night's Forge rows. All of it is computed by var/j203-tools/read.py exactly as written in the pilot

THE ARM is read only when complete, by the first row that holds, exactly one reading: SHOWN when lo > 0.5 and elo >= 15; INCONCLUSIVE when not SHOWN and eloHi >= 15 (case 1 included); NOT SHOWN, indistinguishable when eloHi < 15, eloLo < 0 < eloHi and eloLo > -15; NOT SHOWN, no weaker when eloHi < 15 and eloLo >= 0 (case 2); NOT SHOWN, loses badly when eloHi < -15; NOT SHOWN, worse, not badly otherwise (tooWide and case 3 included). A candidate is SHOWN, INCONCLUSIVE, indistinguishable or no weaker. WHAT FOLLOWS, only when the match is complete, exactly one (follows 1): confirm when the arm is a candidate (closesAsReachedIfHolds 1: a holding confirmation closes the track as reached); trackCloses (and closing) otherwise. repost is 1 when the match is not complete; then follows is 0 and nothing follows from the night. EVERY CHECKED VALUE IS A NUMBER: every flag is 0 or 1, margin 40, the mix counters per decision numbers (0 when unread), and no check compares with null or with a string. selfPlayOpens and liveSeatChanged are 0 in every reading of this night. Reported beside, deciding nothing, each labelled as across D533's merge (which changes bridge/src and by D533 point 3 leaves every earlier value's play unchanged) and, when the blocks are not exactly 114,900,000-114,900,149 with every game (chainDeals 0), as across deals: the arm minus J208's arm at the same margin (search-v2-rrandom4them-m40: the mix's own effect) and minus J208's other arm, minus J206's arm (search-v2-rrandom4them-lcb-m40) and minus J202's arm at the same margin (search-v2-rrandom4-m40, both seats random), the arm minus J204 (b)'s policy-outlet with D528's hw and interval (no reading, no replay, no count); each side's ms per decision (p + a + b, and by kind), rollouts and rounds per searched decision and their ratio, play and copy ms a rollout, the decisions decided on fewer than two rounds, rollout errors and step caps; the arm's Forge and random rounds and rollouts per mix decision, the best alternative's paired differences by kind (pairs and mean, in leaf points) and the share of decisions whose two kinds disagreed in sign (a rate, never which kind was right); every search.rr.* counter per random rollout and per game (the opponent's random seat in the random rounds alone); searched and changed decisions by kind and the priority overrides by direction (from a pass, to another play, to a pass) as shares beside J208's, J206's and J202's; budget fallbacks with their interval and other fallbacks; the deal blocks played; the arm's ten longest and ten quickest lost games with their counters. title: Where the search's strength is, by decision kind (D535, config only, no new Java): search-v2 with each of priority, attacks and blocks searched or left to Forge, all eight combinations, each one fixed 1,200-game match (600 mirrored pairs, D398, the confirm set, no stopping rule) against forge-default on the same 600 deals, each in a ladder folder of its own, read paired by deal (WHOLE, ALONE and LAST for each kind, INTERACTION, REPLICATION against J194 (a)'s rows) and by D535's faster-seat candidate rule; alone on the machine
decides: D535 points 5 and 6, from the night's eight match lines and their rows, paired by deal (D535 point 4), every threshold compared in ten-thousandths of score. WHOLE = the all corner's pair score minus the none corner's, the search's whole gain: its lower end not above 0 means something is broken, nothing else is read and the night is diagnosed first. ALONE for each of priority, attacks and blocks (only-k minus none): ADDS ALONE, HURTS ALONE or NOT SHOWN ALONE. LAST for each (all minus no-k): NEEDED, HURTS or NOT SHOWN NEEDED. INTERACTION and REPLICATION (all minus J194 (a)'s rows) are information only. The faster-seat candidate rule: a partial arm X is a candidate when all minus X has its point at or under +0.014 score with WHOLE above 0; among several the one with the least search time a game is taken forward, and it earns a 4,800-game head-to-head against search-v1-anytime as its own job under its own decision (J198's shape). No candidate is the expected reading: the table then says where the next lane's compute goes (D535 point 7). No reading of this night changes the live seat (D509: a seat-queue row and the owner's)
hypothesis: none registered on any reading. What is known, on these deals: J194 (a) search-v1-anytime (search-v2) against forge-default 0.6233 [0.6023, 0.6444], +87.5 Elo [72.1, 103.2], 1,200 games at pin 72302c69, 29,179 searched decisions (20,434 priority, 6,839 attacks, 1,906 blocks; 4,004, 1,073 and 304 changed: 19.6%, 15.7%, 15.9%), so priority is about 70% of the seat's thinking time, attacks about 23% and blocks about 6.4%; J204 (b) policy-outlet (search-v2's seat with the search off) against search-v2 head to head -84.4 Elo [-99.9, -69.3]. No match of any of the six partial arms has been played, and what= has been pab in every search player before them. Expected, not registered (D535 point 7): no faster-seat candidate. The paired comparison's own noise, measured on this host's earlier matches on these deals before any game of this night: two search seats' pair scores correlate at about 0.45 to 0.55 and the difference's 95% half-width is about 0.020 to 0.022 in score, about 15 to 16 Elo; a search seat against a seat without search correlates at 0.09 to 0.21, about 0.026 to 0.028. The night resolves differences of about 16 to 20 Elo and no finer
rule: written 2026-11-10 before any rated game of any of the six partial arms, word for word as D535 states it (its points 5 and 6; D535's bold dropped): "5. The readings, written before any game of the night. `none`, `only-k`, `no-k` and `all` are the corners of point 1; k is one of p, a, b. - WHOLE = Δ(all, none): the search's whole gain on these deals. If its lower end is not above 0, something is broken (J204 (b) measured search-v2 84 Elo above `policy-outlet` head to head): nothing else is read and the night is diagnosed first. - ALONE(k) = Δ(only-k, none): what searching kind k adds when nothing else is searched. `ADDS ALONE` when its lower end is above 0; `HURTS ALONE` when its upper end is below 0; otherwise `NOT SHOWN ALONE`. - LAST(k) = Δ(all, no-k): what searching kind k adds when the other two are searched already, which is what the live seat would lose by not searching it. `NEEDED` when its lower end is above 0; `HURTS` when its upper end is below 0; otherwise `NOT SHOWN NEEDED`. - INTERACTION (information only) = the mean over deals of all − only-p − only-a − only-b + 2 × none: above 0, the kinds help each other; below, they overlap. - REPLICATION (information only) = Δ(all, J194 (a)'s rows): the same config on the same deals at two pins and five days apart. It is the paired comparison's own noise floor, and the one place where the code under search-v2 between `72302c69` and this night's pin would show. An interval that includes 0 is never worded as "no effect". 6. The faster-seat candidate rule. The six partial arms (`only-p`, `only-a`, `only-b`, `no-p`, `no-a`, `no-b`) are each read against `all`: an arm X is a faster-seat candidate when Δ(all, X)'s point is at most +0.014 in score (about 10 Elo at these scores: the bar J198 used), WHOLE's interval being wholly above 0 (point 5's reading). Among several candidates the one taken forward is the one with the least search time a game on its own match line (`aSearch.msPerDecision × aSearch.searched / played`). A candidate is not a result: at this night's ± 16 Elo an arm truly 20 Elo worse passes about one time in nine (a standard error of about 8 Elo, the bar 10 Elo under the truth). It earns a 4,800-game head-to-head against `search-v1-anytime`, as its own job under its own decision, in J198's shape (the −10 Elo bar, D519's four readings). A seat change is never made by this decision or that one: it is a seat-queue row and the owner's (D509)."
publicTitle: Which decisions make the search strong: priority, attacks or blocks
publicDecides: Where the search gets its strength, and whether a faster seat is worth testing

title: The no-block seat: one fixed 4,800-game match (2,400 mirrored pairs, D398, the confirm set, no stopping rule) of search-v2-no-b, search-v2 searching priority and attack decisions and leaving blocks to Forge, against search-v1-anytime (search-v2, the live seat, searching all three), on deal blocks no match has played (--host j211, 931,900,000-931,900,599), with D536's pre-registered reading: NO-BLOCK SEAT HOLDS, NO-BLOCK SEAT FAILS or INCONCLUSIVE AT 4,800. This job never changes the live seat
decides: whether search-v2 without its block search (what=pa, `search-v2-no-b`) is at most 10 Elo weaker than search-v2 (what=pab, `search-v1-anytime`, the live seat), measured head to head with 95% confidence at 4,800 games on deals neither has played (D536 points 5 to 9). NO-BLOCK SEAT HOLDS makes search-v2-no-b a live-seat candidate: a seat-queue row with the measured point, interval and seconds saved, for the owner's one word (D509), never this job's change. NO-BLOCK SEAT FAILS says the block search is worth more than 10 Elo head to head; the arm stays registered and is not retried. INCONCLUSIVE AT 4,800: not adopted and not played again. Whatever the reading, the match is the sharpest measure there is of what the block search is worth (about +-5 Elo against J210's +-12 by deal), the next lane reads it, and this job never changes the live seat: SearchConfig.LIVE_DEFAULTS stays `what=pab`
hypothesis: J210 (D535; 1,200 games each against forge-default on the same 600 deals) read search-v2-no-b +88.1 Elo [72.9, 103.7] and search-v1-anytime +89.4 [73.9, 105.1], and the block search's paired contribution on top of the other two kinds (LAST b) +0.0017 score [-0.0148, +0.0182], about +1.2 Elo [-11, +13] against Forge, NOT SHOWN NEEDED, where priority's was +0.0742 and attacks' +0.0342. Searching blocks alone was worth +0.0158 over no search (ALONE b), so the block search is not nothing, and against search-v2 itself (which attacks by search) it may be worth more or less than against Forge: nothing here predicts the sign. If the true head-to-head difference is near J210's point (about -1 Elo for the arm), an interval of about +-5 Elo (J198: +-5.2; J197: +-5.0) reads HOLDS about 9 times in 10 (a standard error of about 2.6 Elo; HOLDS needs a point above about -5). FAILS needs a point below about -15, and a true -10 reads HOLDS about 2.5% of the time. The arm searched 22.7 decisions a game against 24.3 and spent 20.9 against 22.7 search seconds a game in J210 (x0.92): the saving, if it holds, is about 1.8 s a game, 8%, not the half J198 asked about
rule: D536 point 7, merged before any J211 game was played (written 2026-11-11 after J210, whose table named the arm), in its words (its list set as sentences): "the match is **complete** when its two names and hashes are A's and B's in that order, `complete` is true, 4,800 games were played and errors plus timeouts are at most 240, its blocks are exactly 931,900,000–931,900,599, and A's side searched no block decision while searching priority and attacks. NO-BLOCK SEAT HOLDS: complete and the interval's lower end is above −10 Elo. NO-BLOCK SEAT FAILS: complete and the interval's upper end is below −10 Elo. INCONCLUSIVE AT 4,800: complete and neither. Three words describe the interval beside the verdict and decide nothing: indistinguishable when it holds 0, a measured loss when it is wholly below 0, a measured gain when wholly above. A HOLDS that is also a measured loss is reported as both (holds the bar and loses about N)." The ends are the match line's own eloLo and eloHi, which the ladder rounds to 0.1 Elo, so a printed -10.0 is not above -10 and not below it. The bar is J198's and D517's "at most 10 Elo weaker", named for this match in D535 point 6 before the candidate was known. D519's reading of the same line (SHOWN, SMALL GAIN, INCONCLUSIVE AT 4,800 or NOT SHOWN, for the arm as a gain over search-v2) is printed beside the verdict as information and decides nothing. An incomplete match gets no verdict. J210's numbers stand beside it as a description and are never pooled with it. title: The search's horizon (D537, config only, no play change): three fixed 1,200-game matches (600 mirrored pairs each, D398, the confirm set, no stopping rule) of search-v2 with its rollouts played one turn further against search-v1-anytime (search-v2, the live seat), each in a ladder folder of its own on blocks 114,900,000-114,900,149 -- search-v2-t1 (priority and block rollouts to the end of the next turn at 1.5 s), search-v2-a1 (attack rollouts one turn further at 1.5 s), search-v2-t1-x3 (t1 at 4.5 s, the round cap still 12) -- each read by D519's four readings at 1,200 games, pre-registered in D537; then, information only, 720 recorded games of search-v2 against Forge Default summarised. This job never changes the live seat
decides: D537 points 6 and 7, from each arm's own match line alone. Each match against search-v1-anytime reads exactly one of D519's four readings at 1,200 games: SHOWN (lo > 0.5 and elo >= +15), SMALL GAIN (lo > 0.5 and elo < +15), INCONCLUSIVE AT 1,200 (lo <= 0.5 and eloHi >= +15), NOT SHOWN (lo <= 0.5 and eloHi < +15). A SHOWN or SMALL GAIN arm is a candidate for one 4,800-game confirmation against search-v1-anytime on deals no match has played, as its own job under its own decision; INCONCLUSIVE AT 1,200 is information; a NOT SHOWN arm is not played again. Nothing is adopted from 1,200 games and this job never changes the live seat (D509): SearchConfig.LIVE_DEFAULTS stays anytime=1 at turns=0. D537 point 8 says, as consequences and not rules, what the three readings together point at (the horizon pays at search-v2's clock; pays per rollout but not per second; pays for attacks; or is closed for Forge rollouts at this leaf). The recording step decides nothing
hypothesis: none registered on any reading. What is known: search-v2's rollouts end with the turn the decision is made in (turns=0: the AI's own for a play or an attack, the opponent's for a block), so the reply to a play or an attack is never played; with turns=1 a block's rollout plays the AI's own next turn. D312's pilot (October, the fixed-round search) put one more turn at about three times a rollout's cost with 53% budget fallbacks at 1.5 s; it was never played. D351's aturns=1 on the fixed-three-round search (search-v1-fixed3-aturns1) SPRT-stopped at 50.2% over 488 games; never played on the anytime search. More clock at turns=0 bought nothing (x0.25 -14.5, x0.5 -4.6 and at 4,800 games -6.5 [-11.7, -1.3], x2 -4.1, x4 +1.7 [-6.7, +10.2] Elo; J194, J195, J198). On these deals against Forge Default (J210's pab corner) search-v2 ran 15.17 rollouts a searched decision at 53.4 ms of play each and its attacks alone (only-a corner) 11.09 at 85.9 ms. Expected, not registered (D537 point 4): t1 at 1.5 s decides most alternatives on one or two paired rounds (the anytime loop prunes to what the time left carries), so its reading is the horizon plus thinner evidence; t1-x3 is the horizon at about search-v2's evidence a decision. Each reading's noise: the arm's own interval about +-11 Elo at 1,200 games (J209: -6.9 [-17.8, +3.9])
rule: D537 points 6 and 7, merged before any J212 game was played (written 2026-11-11 while J211 played), in their words (D537's bold dropped, its list set as sentences): "A match is complete when its line names the arm and search-v1-anytime in that order at their hashes, says complete: true, played all 1,200 games with errors plus timeouts at most 60, carries score, lo, elo, eloLo and eloHi, was played on exactly blocks 114,900,000-114,900,149 with no other match's game in its folder, every batch line carried the two seat configs of point 1 exactly, and both sides searched priority, attack and block decisions. Exactly one reading of a complete match, in this precedence, compared as the line carries them (lo in integer ten-thousandths, Elo in integer tenths): SHOWN: lo above 0.5 and elo at least +15; SMALL GAIN: lo above 0.5 and elo below +15; INCONCLUSIVE AT 1,200: lo at most 0.5 and eloHi at least +15; NOT SHOWN: lo at most 0.5 and eloHi below +15. An incomplete match gets no reading and is reposted alone under a new job id. Beside each reading, deciding nothing: indistinguishable (the Elo interval holds 0), a measured loss (wholly below), a measured gain (wholly above). ... A SHOWN or SMALL GAIN arm is a candidate for one 4,800-game confirmation against search-v1-anytime on deals no match has played (a host name of its own, as D536 point 6 did), under D519's readings, as its own job under its own decision; nothing is adopted from 1,200 games. An INCONCLUSIVE AT 1,200 is information and is not confirmed by this decision. A NOT SHOWN arm is not played again. No reading changes the live seat (D509)." The arms: search-v2-t1 (63c35e9f7d5b), search-v2-a1 (3cf65e94df28), search-v2-t1-x3 (ce99b41f9898), each A against B = search-v1-anytime (cdd55e02a89c). Each arm is read on its own match; the three are never pooled and no arm is read against another. The cost, the horizon's trace and the recording are reported and change no reading
